text:
A 60 HP electric motor lifts an elevator having a maximum total load capacity of 2000 kg. If the frictional force on the elevator is 4000 N, the speed of the elevator at full load is close to : 
$(1 HP = 746 W, g = 10 ms^{-2})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
F = mg + f

F = 20000 + 4000 = 24000 N

We know, Power(P) = Fv

$\Rightarrow$ v = $\frac{P}{F}$ = $\frac{60\times 746}{24000}$

$\Rightarrow$ v $\approx$ 1.9 m/s
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot

text:
A long solenoid of radius R carries a time (t) - dependent current 
$I(t)=I_{0}t(1 - t). A$ ring of radius 2R is placed coaxially near its middle. During the time interval 0 $\leq$ t $\leq$ 1, the induced current $(I_{R})$ and the induced EMF$(V_{R})$ in the ring change as :
options: Direction of $I_{R}$ remains unchanged and $V_{R}$ is zero at t = 0.25
Direction of $I_{R}$ remains unchanged and $V_{R}$ is maximum at t = 0.5
At t = 0.25 direction of $I_{R}$ reverses and $V_{R}$ is maximum
At t = 0.5 direction of $I_{R}$ reverses and $V_{R}$ is zero
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$I(t) = I_{0}t(1 - t)$

We know, $𝜙$ = BA

$\Rightarrow$ $𝜙$ = $μ_{0}$nIA

$\Rightarrow$ $𝜙$ = $μ_{0}$nAI$_{0}(t - t^{2})$

Also $V_{R} =$ $-\frac{d𝜙}{dt}$

= - $μ_{0}$nAI$_{0}(1 - 2t)$

$V_{R} = 0$ when 1 - 2t = 0

$\Rightarrow$ t = 0.5

Also we know, $V_{R} = I_{R}r$

$\Rightarrow$ $I_{R} =$ $\frac{μ_{0}nAI_{0}(1-2t)}{r}$

after $t = 0.5, I_{R}$ reverses its direction.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot

Two infinite planes each with uniform surface charge density $σ$ are kept in such a way that the angle between them is $30^{o}$. The electric field in the region shown between them is given by :

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Electric field due to each sheet is uniform and
equal to E = $\frac{σ}{2ε_{0}}$

$\therefore$ Electric field along y direction

 = $\left (\frac{σ}{2ε_{0}}-\frac{σ}{2ε_{0}}\sin 60^{\circ }\right )\hat{y}$

Also Electric field along x direction

= - $\frac{σ}{2ε_{0}}\cos 60^{\circ }\widehat{x}$

= $-\frac{σ}{4ε_{0}}\widehat{x}$ + $\frac{σ}{2ε_{0}}\left (1-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right )\hat{y}$

= $\frac{σ}{2\in _{0}}\left [\left (1-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right )\hat{y}-\frac{\widehat{x}}{2}\right ]$

text: Speed of a transverse wave on a straight wire (mass 6.0 g, length 60 cm and area of cross-section $1.0 mm^{2})$ is $90 ms^{-1}$. If the Young's modulus of wire is 16 $\times$ $10^{11} Nm^{-2}$, the extension of wire over its natural length is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Velocity of the wave, v = $\sqrt{\frac{T}{μ}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $T = v^{2}μ$

We know, Young's modulus, 

Y = $\frac{\frac{F}{A}}{\frac{\Delta l}{l}}$ = $\frac{\frac{T}{A}}{\frac{\Delta l}{l}}$

[As here F = T]

$\Rightarrow$ $Y\frac{\Delta l}{l}$ = $\frac{T}{A}$ = $\frac{v^{2}μ}{A}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta$l = $\frac{v^{2}μl}{AY}$

= $\frac{90\times 90\times \frac{6\times 10-3}{60\times 10-2}\times 60\times 10^{-2}}{1\times 10^{-6}\times 16\times 10^{11}}$

= 3 $\times$ $10^{-5} m$

 = 0.03 mm
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot

text: The time period of revolution of electron in its ground state orbit in a hydrogen atom is 1.6 $\times$ $10^{-16} s$. The frequency of revolution of the electron in its first excited state (in $s^{-1})$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Time period of revolution of electron in $n^{th}$ orbit

V = $\frac{2πr}{V}$

= $\frac{2πa_{0}\left (\frac{n2}{Z}\right )}{V_{0}\left (\frac{Z}{n}\right )}$

$\Rightarrow$ T $\propto$ $\frac{n^{3}}{Z^{2}}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{T_{1}}{T_{2}}=\frac{n_{1}^{3}}{n_{2}^{3}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1.6\times 10^{-16}}{T_{2}}=\frac{1}{(2)^{3}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $T_{2} = 1.6$ $\times$ 8 $\times$ $10^{-16}$

$\therefore$ $f_{2} =$ $\frac{1}{T_{2}}$ = $\frac{1}{1.6\times 8\times 10^{-16}}$ = 7.8 $\times$ $10^{14}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot

text:
A satellite of mass m is launched vertically upwards with an initial speed u from the surface of the earth. After it reaches height R (R = radius of the earth), it ejects a rocket
of mass $\frac{m}{10}$
so that subsequently the
satellite moves in a circular orbit. The kinetic energy of the rocket is (G is the gravitational constant; M is the mass of the earth) :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Using energy conservation

$K_{i} + U_{i} = K_{f} + U_{f}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{2}mu^{2}-\frac{GmM}{R}$ = $\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}-\frac{GmM}{2R}$

$\Rightarrow$ v = $\sqrt{u^{2}-\frac{GM}{R}}$

[IMG]


After ejecting a rocket of mass $\frac{m}{10}$ the remaining part of mass $\frac{9m}{10}$ will rotate the earth with orbital velocity $v_{0}$.

$\therefore$ $v_{0} =$ $\sqrt{\frac{GM}{2R}}$

Applying momentum conservation along radial direction,

Before firing rocket momentum of satellite in radial direction = mv

And after firing rocket momentum of satellite in radial direction = 0 and momentum of rocket in radial direction = $\frac{m}{10}v_{2}$

$\therefore$ mv = $\frac{m}{10}v_{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $v_{2} = 10v$

Now applying momentum conservation along tangential direction we get,

 0 = $\frac{m}{10}v_{1}$ - $\frac{9m}{10}v_{0}$

$\Rightarrow\frac{9m}{10}v_{0}$ = $\frac{m}{10}v_{1}$

$\Rightarrow$ $v_{1} = 9v_{0}$

$\therefore$Total Kinetic Energy of rocket 

= $\frac{1}{2}\frac{m}{10}\left (v_{1}^{2}+v_{2}^{2}\right )$

= $\frac{1}{2}\frac{m}{10}\left (81v_{0}^{2}+100v^{2}\right )$

= $\frac{m}{20}\left (81\left (\frac{GM}{2R}\right )+100\left (u^{2}-\frac{GM}{R}\right )\right )$

= $\frac{m}{20}\left (100u^{2}+\frac{81GM}{2R}-\frac{100GM}{R}\right )$

= $\frac{m}{20}\left (100u^{2}-\frac{119GM}{2R}\right )$

= $5m\left (u^{2}-\frac{119GM}{200R}\right )$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot

text: A LCR circuit behaves like a damped harmonic oscillator. Comparing it with a physical spring-mass damped oscillator having damping constant 'b', the correct equivalence would be:
options: L $\leftrightarrow$ k, C $\leftrightarrow$ b, R $\leftrightarrow$ m
L $\leftrightarrow$ m, C $\leftrightarrow$ k, R $\leftrightarrow$ b
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For spring mass damped oscillator

ma = - kx - bv

$\Rightarrow$ ma + kx + bv = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $m\frac{d^{2}x}{dt^{2}}$ + b$\frac{dx}{dt}$ + kx = 0 ....(1)

For LCR circuit

L$\frac{di}{dt}$ + iR + $\frac{q}{C}$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ L$\frac{d^{2}q}{dt^{2}}$ + R$\frac{dq}{dt}$ + $\frac{q}{C}$ = 0 .....(2)

Comparing (1) and (2), we get

L $\leftrightarrow$ m, C $\leftrightarrow$ $\frac{1}{k}$, R $\leftrightarrow$ b
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot

A parallel plate capacitor has plates of area A separated by distance 'd' between them. It is filled with a dielectric which has a dielectric constant that varies as k(x) = K(1 + $α$x) where 'x' is the distance measured from one of the plates. If (ad) << 1, the total capacitance of the system is best given by the expression :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
k(x) = K(1 + $α$x)

[IMG]


Capacitance of element $dC_{1} =$ $\frac{Kε_{0}A}{dx}$ = $\frac{K(1+αx)ε_{0}A}{dx}$

$\frac{1}{C_{eq}}$ = $\int \frac{1}{dC_{1}}$

= $\int\limits _{0}^{d}\frac{dx}{KA(1+αx)ε_{0}}$

= $\frac{1}{KAαε_{0}}\ln (1+αx)$

Using expansion of ln (1 + x) keeping x $\ll$ 1

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{C_{eq}}$ = $\frac{1}{KAαε_{0}}\left (αd-\frac{α^{2}d^{2}}{2}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $C_{eq} =$ $\frac{ε_{0}KA}{d}\left (1-\frac{αd}{2}\right )^{-1}$

$\Rightarrow$ $C_{eq} =$ $\frac{ε_{0}KA}{d}\left (1+\frac{αd}{2}\right )$

text:
A beam of electromagnetic radiation of intensity $6.4 × 10^{–5} W/cm^{2}$ is comprised of wavelength,
$λ$ = 310 nm. It falls normally on a metal (work function $𝜙$ = 2eV) of surface area of $1 cm^{2}$. If one
in $10^{3}$ photons ejects an electron, total number of electrons ejected in 1 s is $10^{x}. (hc = 1240$ eVnm,
$1eV = 1.6 × 10^{–19} J)$, then x is $_____$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Photon energy: $E=\dfrac{hc}{λ}=\dfrac{1240\text{eV nm}}{310\text{nm}}=4\text{eV}=4\times 1.6\times 10^{-19}\text{J}=6.4\times 10^{-19}\text{J}$, which exceeds $𝜙=2\text{eV}$, so photoemission occurs.

Power falling on the surface: $P=IA=\left (6.4\times 10^{-5}\text{W cm}^{-2}\right )\left (1\text{cm}^{2}\right )=6.4\times 10^{-5}\text{W}$.

Photons striking per second:

$N=\dfrac{P}{E}=\dfrac{6.4\times 10^{-5}}{6.4\times 10^{-19}}=10^{14}\text{s}^{-1}$

One photon in $10^{3}$ ejects an electron, so electrons ejected in 1 s $=\dfrac{10^{14}}{10^{3}}=10^{11}$, giving $x=11$.

Hence, the answer is 11.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot

text:
A loop ABCDEFA of straight edges has six corner points A(0, 0, 0), B(5, 0, 0), C(5, 5, 0), D (0, 5,
0), E(0, 5, 5) and F(0, 0, 5). The magnetic field in this region is $\vec{B}=\left (3\hat{i}+4\widehat{k}\right )T$
. The quantity of
flux through the loop ABCDEFA (in Wb) is $_______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Adding the edge $AD$ in both directions splits the loop $ABCDEFA$ into two squares of side $5\text{m}$: $ABCDA$ in the plane $z=0$ and $ADEFA$ in the plane $x=0$.

For $ABCDA$, $A\to B$ is along $+\hat{i}$ and $B\to C$ along $+\hat{j}$, so its area vector is along $\hat{i}\times \hat{j}=\hat{k}$: $⃗{A}_{1}=25\hat{k}\text{m}^{2}$.

For $ADEFA$, $A\to D$ is along $+\hat{j}$ and $D\to E$ along $+\hat{k}$, so its area vector is along $\hat{j}\times \hat{k}=\hat{i}$: $⃗{A}_{2}=25\hat{i}\text{m}^{2}$.

$⃗{A}=⃗{A}_{1}+⃗{A}_{2}=(25\hat{i}+25\hat{k})\text{m}^{2}$

$𝜙=⃗{B}\cdot ⃗{A}=(3\hat{i}+4\hat{k})\cdot (25\hat{i}+25\hat{k})=75+100=175\text{Wb}$

Hence, the answer is 175.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot
